Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one member to serve as Chairperson and one member to serve as Vice Chairperson for
the term ending on June 30, 2026.

Background
Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) Sections 2.40.050(A) and (B), Vernon Housing
Commission (VHC) members are required to elect a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson annually
from different appointing categories. Additionally, a commissioner may not serve as Chairperson
for more than two consecutive terms. The VMC is silent on term limits for the Vice Chairperson.

The VHC consists of seven members, including three residents (one who shall be a member of
the City Council), three business representatives, and one employee of a business located in
Vernon. Members serve for a term of four years and can serve no more than two consecutive full
four-year terms.

Commissioner Nevarez Jr. was elected to a first term as Chairperson on September 11, 2024,
and is eligible to serve a second term. Due to a term expiration, the position of Vice Chair is
vacant.

The current members are as follows:

  Commissioner  Appointing Category  Date Appointed  End of Term
Jacquie Cabrera  Business Representative  August 5, 2025  June 30, 2029
Ronit Edry  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Jorge Nevarez Jr.  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Bertha Padilla  Employee of a Business  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Leticia Lopez  Resident (Council Member)  August 5, 2025  June 30, 2029
Ulisses Sanchez  Resident  August 5, 2025  June 30, 2029
Marlene Ybarra  Resident  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027

All members of the Commission are eligible to serve as Chairperson or Vice Chairperson. The
Commission should select a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson from different appointing
categories to serve an annual term through June 30, 2026.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Submitted by:  Daniel S. Wall, P.E., Director of Public Works

Subject
Retaining Specialized Property Management Administrative Services

Recommendation
Authorize the Commission Director or their designee, to solicit proposals, evaluate submissions,
and seek City Council approval for an agreement with a qualified firm to provide property
management administrative services for the City’s rental housing program as necessary.

Background
The City owns and operates 26 rental housing units. These properties are subject to a broad
range of state and federal housing laws, including California’s Fair Housing regulations, U.S.
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) requirements, and a multitude of tenant
protection statutes. In recent years, these laws have undergone substantial and frequent
changes. Staying current with these requirements demands specialized expertise in property
management, compliance auditing, rent-setting protocols, income certification, and tenant
relations.

Currently, administrative functions are handled in-house. However, internal reviews and legal
counsel feedback have identified compliance risks due to evolving and increasingly complex
regulations, and limited staffing capacity. Therefore, it is recommended that the City retain
specialized administrative services pertaining to City owned rental housing.

Retaining a firm to provide specialized administrative services would:
  • Ensure continuous compliance with state and federal housing laws;
  • Reduce the City’s exposure to legal and financial liabilities; and
  • Provide tenants with consistent, professional management services.

In addition to the above services, the selected firm will be required to:
  • Maintain detailed records in compliance with the City’s retention schedules;
  • Provide quarterly reports to the VHC;
  • Coordinate with the City Attorney on legal matters concerning City-owned housing; and
  • Ensure that VHC Policies and Procedures are adhered to.

Given the dynamic nature of housing laws, retaining specialized property management services
for City-owned housing is a proactive measure that will protect the City’s interests, ensure
compliance with housing laws, and maintain high-quality services for tenants. As such, it is
recommended that the VHC authorize staff to move forward with the process of procuring the
services of a qualified property management firm.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

None.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Chairperson Nevarez invited questions from the Commission.

  In response to a question from Commissioner Sanchez regarding the timeline for
  the vacant property on Furlong to be ready for the lottery process, Public Works
  Director Wall explained the unit was undergoing the early stages of clean-up,
  inspections, and renovations, and there was not an expected timeline for
  completion.

  Chairperson Nevarez inquired about a potential transfer and Public Works Director
  Wall explained the transfer process. He stated that if there were multiple
  applications for tenant transfers to the vacant unit, then a tenant transfer lottery
  would be conducted. Director Wall further explained that if there were no tenants
  interested in a transfer, then a normal lottery would be conducted for the vacant
  unit.

  Nevarez called for a motion.
